title: Working as a Bartender
summary: Expectations and responsibilities of a bartender in a fast-paced environment.
content: Your job isn't just pouring drinks. It’s about flow, sharp timing, and reading the room. The guest sees confidence and control before they even taste the product. You’re expected to work clean, smart, and fast; know your drinks; handle glassware properly; and keep the bar tight.

title: Responsible Bartending
summary: Understanding alcohol laws, safe service, and being a responsible host.
content: Know when and how to refuse service. Be aware of alcohol strength, guest behaviour, and legal limits. Monitor intoxication levels, and intervene early. A responsible bartender protects the venue, the guest, and the team.

title: Alcohol, ID, and Measures
summary: Alcohol laws, checking ID, and standardised pouring practices.
content: Learn the correct ID procedures. Understand standard measures and how to pour accurately. Ensure every drink is legal, consistent, and up to house standards. Never serve underage or intoxicated guests.

title: Guest Interaction & Memory
summary: Memorable service starts with strong guest recognition and clear communication.
content: Use guest names when possible, remember orders, and acknowledge returning guests. Repetition, verbal confirmation, and structured routines boost memory and trust.

title: Shift Standards
summary: Opening, mid-shift, and closing routines to keep operations tight.
content: Always show up 15 minutes early. Pre-shift tasks include glass polish, ice levels, and bar prep. Post-shift means clean-down, fridges, till-out, and team handovers. Don’t leave mess for the next shift.

title: Hygiene & Setup
summary: Station prep, cleanliness routines, and health standards.
content: Surfaces must be sanitised before every shift. Ice scoops, fruit, and tools must be hygienic. No drinks without a clean station. Learn colour-coded cloth systems and weekly deep-clean routines.

title: Tools & Glassware
summary: Learn the essential tools and how to use glassware correctly.
content: Know your tins, strainers, jiggers, and stirring tools. Glassware must be handled by the stem or base only. No hands inside. Learn to identify and polish coupe, highball, rocks, Nick & Nora, and wine glasses.

title: Method & Technique
summary: Master the basics: build, shake, stir, strain, and layer.
content: Each method has a purpose: shaking for aeration, stirring for clarity, building for simplicity. Learn when to fine strain and when to double shake. Practice clean, elegant technique with zero spillage.

title: Roundbuilding & Service Flow
summary: Building rounds efficiently and managing service under pressure.
content: Start with long drinks, finish with shaken ones. Build rounds from easiest to hardest. Communicate clearly, check dockets fast, and delegate where needed. Efficiency is teamwork plus anticipation.

title: Bar Prep & Rota Systems
summary: Understanding prep lists, rotation systems, and stock duties.
content: Each shift has designated prep: syrups, juices, garnishes, batching. Know your duties. Rota systems should be followed precisely. Label, rotate, and manage waste properly. Restock before the next shift, not after.

title: Cocktail Specs & Batching
summary: How we learn and follow cocktail specs in service.
content: Every cocktail has a reason and a ratio. Specs must be memorised and followed unless otherwise instructed. Use jiggers, taste test when appropriate, and record new drinks into the spec book or digital system.

title: Zero ABV & Inclusive Service
summary: Serving guests who don’t drink alcohol with the same quality and flair.
content: Zero-alcohol drinks are not an afterthought. Learn the zero-ABV menu, use proper garnishes, and ensure consistent presentation. Offer tastings, upsell creatively, and avoid judgmental language.
